subject: Production WebSocket disconnects — high error rate (Phalanx AI)
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@phalanx.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Phalanx AI Support <support@phalanx.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production WebSocket disconnects — high error rate

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing a production-wide surge in WebSocket disconnects around 06:30 UTC this morning. Symptoms: ~5-10% of active sessions time out after an initial stream (30-90s) and then no further chunks are delivered. Clients get an ERR_STREAM_TIMEOUT on the finalization path. Overall request latency also spikes — median token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s on affected requests.

Impact: several customers (including us) reported partial responses in downstream UIs; our retry logic hits a lot of 502/504s. We’ve attached a session dump and a tarball with capture logs (phalanx-session-dump-0725.jsonl, capture-logs.tar.gz). Sample request ids in the dump: phx-req-8a3f, phx-req-8a4b.

What we need immediately:
- A hot triage call with Redwood engineering now.
- If a rollback or routing change is possible, we’d like it applied as a short-term mitigation.
- Confirmation that you can force a non-streaming fallback per-tenant until root cause is identified.

This is impacting an active trial and the renewal conversation for Q4 — we’re flagging this as high-priority.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Integrations, Phalanx AI

Attachments: phalanx-session-dump-0725.jsonl, capture-logs.tar.gz
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production WebSocket disconnects — high error rate

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m pulling David (infra) and Monica (CS) in now.

Immediate plan:
- David: can you triage network/proxy changes and confirm whether any recent config pushes correlate with the timeframe? Prioritize request ids phx-req-8a3f and phx-req-8a4b.
- Monica: I’ll coordinate comms with the Phalanx account and prepare an exec one-pager.
- Alex: can you confirm whether the affected sessions are all routed through a single gateway/region? Any timestamps for the exact disconnects in UTC will help.

Potential mitigations to consider (we’ll not apply without coordination):
- Temporary rollback of any proxy keepalive/heartbeat tuning pushed in the last 24h.
- Enable per-tenant non-streaming fallback for Phalanx while we investigate.
- Apply a conservative rate limit / queue cap for new streams from the Phalanx origin pool.

I’ll set up a bridge for the next 15 minutes; if we need exec attention faster, flag it here and I’ll escalate.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production WebSocket disconnects — high error rate

Triage notes (initial):
- Correlation: I’m seeing a proxy config push at 05:58 UTC that reduced the WebSocket ping interval on a subset of our edge gateways (from 30s -> 15s) and changed the proxy keepalive behavior. The timing lines up with the start of customer reports.
- Observable signals: elevated 502/504 counts at edge (gateway-7 and gateway-9), and an increase in long-lived connections being closed by intermediate proxies. We also see chunk gaps in the chunked transfer stream where the server continued to process but the client received no further frames.
- Hypothesis: an intermediate NAT/load-balancer misinterpreting the more aggressive keepalive/ping pattern as idle or malformed frames, dropping connections mid-stream.

Requested artifacts from Phalanx (Alex):
- pcap or tcpdump for an affected session (if available).
- Exact UTC timestamps for a few disconnects — I’ll match them against edge logs.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk, fast):
1) Roll back the edge proxy keepalive change for gateway-7 and gateway-9 to the previous config (30s).
2) Bump server-side application keepalive/heartbeat to 90s so downstream proxies see regular TCP activity.
3) Enable non-stream fallback for Phalanx tenant ID for 2 hours (zero changes to data plane aside from routing).

I’ll prepare a short rollback job and a plan to isolate affected gateways. If rollback is approved I can push within the next 20 minutes.

—David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@phalanx.ai>, Karen Li <karen.li@phalanx.ai>
Date: 2027-07-26T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Phalanx AI — Exec summary and next steps (rollback applied)

Summary (for exec thread):
- Issue: Starting 2027-07-25 06:30 UTC, a subset of WebSocket sessions began experiencing mid-stream silence and eventual timeouts. Customers reported partial responses and client errors (ERR_STREAM_TIMEOUT). Error rate peaked at ~7.3% for Phalanx traffic and token latency on affected sessions increased to ~1.1s.
- Root cause (initial): A proxy config change deployed 05:58 UTC reduced WebSocket ping intervals and altered keepalive behavior; intermediate network elements dropped connections under the new pattern.
- Mitigations applied:
  * 2027-07-25 10:28 UTC — Rolled back edge proxy keepalive/ping settings on gateway-7 and gateway-9.
  * 2027-07-25 10:34 UTC — Bumped server-side keepalive to 90s for affected routing pool.
  * 2027-07-25 10:40 UTC — Enabled non-streaming fallback for Phalanx tenant for 2 hours while we validated stability.
- Current status: Error rate for Phalanx traffic returned to baseline (~0.6%) by 2027-07-25 11:20 UTC. No further production-scale disconnects observed since mitigations. We continue to monitor edge gateway metrics and client session traces.
- Customer impact: brief service degradation window ~06:30–11:20 UTC with partial responses for a subset of users. Phalanx indicated potential renewal sensitivity.

Recommended next steps and asks:
1) Marcus: approve a goodwill credit up to 10% of last month’s invoice for Phalanx (we recommend proactively offering 5% pending their satisfaction).
2) David/infra: schedule a controlled re-deploy of the proxy change behind an internal canary and extended telemetry to ensure intermediaries tolerate the new ping pattern.
3) Monica/CS: share the exec one-pager and a short timeline with Phalanx CTO (Karen) summarizing root cause and mitigation.
4) Ops: retain full capture logs and a pcap from affected sessions in the PHX-1892 folder for 90 days; attach to the HubSpot ticket.

I’m marking this resolved for immediate customer impact; we’ll keep monitoring and will reconvene if we see recurrences. Marcus — please confirm approval for the credit and whether you want us to escalate to the board given the renewal sensitivity.

Thanks all, great triage work.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
